_comment: Meridian Logistics: an ACTIVE DIRECTORY hardening practice box (Windows domain controller; os contains 'win' so nakon uses its powershell deploy path -- SSH transport, Windows OpenSSH, run.ps1 with per-step scripts; elevation comes from the SSH principal, which must be a domain admin here). Every ad-*/gpp-*/gpo-*/ldap-*/firewall-allow configuration is a GENERIC var-driven seed in boxbuilder/vulndb_vuln_configs/; the reused local seeds (weak-password-policy-win, smb1-, audit-, guest-, firewall-disabled, runkey-, scheduled-task-, malicious-service) are the pinecrest generation. ORDER MATTERS: weak-password-policy-win runs FIRST (weak policy + complexity off before weak account passwords are set); users are created before group-adds and before the DCSync ACL (its trustee must exist); gpp-/gpo-persistence create their own GPOs independently. On a DC, `net accounts` reads/writes the DOMAIN policy (this is deliberate: the box teaches Default Domain Policy hardening). Name discipline: every USERNAME / GROUP / ACCOUNT / SPN / RUN_VALUE_NAME / TASK_NAME / SERVICE_NAME / PAYLOAD_PATH / RULE_NAME / GPO_NAME / PASSWORD here MUST match its paired check's collect params in scenario.yaml byte-identically -- nothing cross-validates. The malicious service is a real running service (powershell.exe -File <payload> as BinaryPathName, sc failure auto-restart), scored by process_state on the payload filename fragment (mbdeploy) plus service_state active/enabled -- rename a PAYLOAD_PATH and you must update the matching collect.pattern in scenario.yaml. Guest/audit/smb1/firewall are scored but Guest is planted by guest-enabled-win (verify it flips the DOMAIN Guest on a DC -- if it only touches a local SAM, hardening uses Set-ADUser Guest -Enabled $false); Spooler is scored but NOT planted (running+auto is the Server default -- that insecure default is the finding).
